purpose: Production-ready briefs for the two thinnest THC infographic subjects. Each brief is designed as a complete full-sheet teaching visual, not a simple reference panel.

qualityStandard.visualStyle: academic studio-quality botanical imagery plus precise scientific diagrams; cream and deep-green system; no yellow tint
qualityStandard.text: all labels must be readable, correctly spelled, scientifically accurate, and independently QA-checked
exclusions: decorative cannabis smoke or lifestyle imagery
single-panel reference art presented as an infographic

assets.title: PPFD, DLI & Photoperiod
assets.teachingGoal: Show the difference between source output, crop-plane photon density, daily photon dose, and delivery schedule without implying that equal DLI guarantees equal biology.
requiredPanels: PPF versus PPFD versus DLI definitions with correct units
DLI = PPFD × photoperiod × 0.0036 for constant PPFD and hours
fixture to crop-plane measurement diagram
three equal-DLI schedule examples labeled as mathematically equal daily dose but not necessarily biologically equivalent
measurement checklist: grid, height, photoperiod, canopy change
context box: spectrum, leaf temperature, stage, environment, canopy geometry
sourceNotes: Michigan State University: Daily Light Integral Defined

assets.title: How to Map Canopy Light
assets.teachingGoal: Teach why a measurement grid is more informative than a single center PPFD reading and how to preserve measurement context.
requiredPanels: top-down realistic canopy with numbered measurement grid
center, edge, overlap, and height examples
mean, minimum, maximum, range, and coefficient-of-variation concepts without prescribing a universal target
sensor orientation and crop-plane height diagram
before and after canopy-height change comparison
common error panel: changing sensor height or angle between readings
sourceNotes: Use quantum-sensor manufacturer calibration concepts only as measurement context, not product endorsement
Interpret uniformity statistics together with the spatial map

assets.title: Light Sensors: What Are You Actually Measuring?
assets.teachingGoal: Differentiate photon-flux measurement from wavelength-resolved spectral measurement and expose major measurement limitations.
requiredPanels: quantum sensor versus spectroradiometer comparison
spectral-response concept graphic
cosine-response concept graphic
PAR 400–700 nm as the conventional PPFD band, with separate note that UV and far-red questions may require different measurement approaches
calibration, cleanliness, orientation, temperature, and sensor-age checklist
warning: different instruments can disagree because they measure differently
sourceNotes: Frontiers in Photobiology 2024 discussion of PAR sensors, DLI, and wavelength-resolved spectral measurement
Avoid presenting emerging ePAR definitions as settled universal practice

assets.title: Light-Response Curves, Saturation & Photoinhibition
assets.teachingGoal: Explain why more photons do not create a simple linear growth response and how acclimation and other limiting factors change interpretation.
requiredPanels: conceptual net-photosynthesis versus PPFD curve with compensation and saturation regions
leaf acclimation comparison
protective energy dissipation and non-photochemical quenching concept
persistent excess-light and photoinhibition concept
confounder checklist: leaf temperature, water status, CO2, nutrition, stage, genetics
diagnostic evidence flow from spatial pattern to controlled correction to recovery
sourceNotes: Do not print a universal cannabis saturation threshold

assets.title: Observation → Measurement → Inference
assets.teachingGoal: Teach users to separate what was seen, what was quantified, and what conclusion is being proposed.
requiredPanels: three-layer evidence stack: observation, measurement, inference
worked plant-health example where leaf discoloration is an observation rather than a diagnosis
raw data and units panel
alternative-explanations branch
evidence-strength ladder based on claim specificity, not a universal ranking of methods
footer workflow: locate, describe, contextualize, measure, compare, track
sourceNotes: Keep causal language bounded by the evidence shown

assets.title: Replication vs Subsampling
assets.teachingGoal: Make the experimental unit visually obvious and prevent repeated readings from being mistaken for independent biological replication.
requiredPanels: diagram of multiple leaves measured on one plant versus independent plants receiving treatment
experimental unit definition
subsample definition
pseudoreplication warning
simple nested-data diagram
planning checklist: unit, treatment assignment, replicate count, sampling locations
sourceNotes: University of Minnesota Extension on-farm research guidance: real replicates versus pseudoreplicates

assets.title: Controls, Randomization & Blocking
assets.teachingGoal: Show how comparison design reduces confounding from position and background gradients.
requiredPanels: control versus treatment comparison
bad layout: all treatments assigned to one side of a light or irrigation gradient
better randomized layout
blocked layout across a known environmental gradient
confounding explanation
audit checklist: control, randomization method, block definition, assignment record
sourceNotes: University of Minnesota Extension on-farm research guidance: control treatments, randomization, replication, and field variability

assets.title: Measurement Quality & Uncertainty
assets.teachingGoal: Explain calibration, resolution, repeatability, uncertainty, metadata, and why extra decimal places are not the same as accuracy.
requiredPanels: measurement chain from true condition to sensor to recorded value to interpretation
accuracy versus precision concept without fake numerical data
calibration and drift timeline
repeat suspicious reading decision tree
metadata checklist: instrument, unit, calibration, time, location, sample method
data-integrity rule: preserve raw value and document corrections rather than silently overwriting
sourceNotes: General measurement-science principles; avoid claiming a precision level that the instrument does not support
